faq.q: Which gradient types and output formats can I generate?
faq.a: Four types: linear (with an angle slider), radial (circle or ellipse, nine position options), conic (from an angle) and repeating-linear. You can copy the standard CSS, or convert it to a Tailwind arbitrary-value class, an SCSS variable, or an RGBA-based version where each hex colour is rewritten as rgba(). There are also 30+ built-in presets.

faq.q: Can I use more than two colours?
faq.a: Yes. Click 'Add Color Stop' to add unlimited stops; each has its own colour picker and a 0–100% position slider, and any stop beyond the first two can be removed. The 'Random' button generates 2–4 random stops with a random angle, and 'Save' stores the current gradient (up to 20) in local storage under the savedGrads key.

faq.q: What resolution is the downloaded PNG?
faq.a: 'Download PNG' renders the gradient to a 1920×1080 canvas. It rebuilds the gradient natively on canvas — createLinearGradient using your angle, createRadialGradient centred for radial, and createConicGradient for conic — rather than screenshotting the preview, so the exported colours and stop positions match the CSS.

faq.q: Why does the CSS angle not match what I'd expect mathematically?
faq.a: In CSS, 0deg points up and angles increase clockwise, so 90deg is left-to-right and 180deg is top-to-bottom — different from the usual maths convention. The tool's angle slider follows the CSS rule. If a gradient arrives rotated from what you pictured, that clockwise-from-top convention is usually why.
